member.name: M:Api.Controllers.AuthenticationController.InitiateAccountRecovery(Iam.DomainService.Accounts.RecoveryUserRequest)
member.summary: Initiate account recovery (password reset flow). INVARIANT: This endpoint always returns 200 OK with IsSuccess = true for any well-formed request, regardless of whether the account exists, is active, or has ever been registered. The actual reason (unknown email / inactive user / send failure) is audited server-side only and never exposed in the response. For unknown or inactive users, the service silently routes the request to an activation email instead of a reset email to prevent account enumeration.

member.name: M:Api.Controllers.IamController.GetRolePermissionChangeImpact(Iam.DomainService.Resources.RolePermissionChangeImpactRequest)
member.summary: Previews what assigning or unassigning the given permissions would do, before the caller commits to it.
member.remarks: POST despite being a read: the diff is two id lists, which do not survive a query string at realistic sizes. Guarded by the roles read permission, not mutate-roles -- it changes nothing, and a reader who can open the role should be able to see the consequence of a change before deciding to ask someone else to make it.

member.name: M:Api.Controllers.IamController.IsOrganizationNameAvailable(Iam.DomainService.Resources.RequestModel.IsOrganizationNameAvailableRequest)
member.summary:
Whether an organization name is free, with alternatives when it is not.
Anonymous because it exists for the signup flow, which is itself anonymous: a multi-step signup can check the name on the organization step instead of failing the user at final submit. This matches the posture of GET iam/email/available.
Advisory only — nothing is reserved, so a name reported available can still be taken by the time signup runs. The authoritative check stays in CreateOrganizationAsync, and the signup response carries suggestions of its own for exactly that race.
Gated on multi-organization mode, like every other organization operation: a tenant that cannot create organizations gets multi_org_disabled rather than an answer.

member.name: M:Blocks.Api.Controllers.AuthorizationController.BuildCallbackFailure(Authentication.DomainService.Oidc.Services.OidcCallbackResult)
member.summary: A failed provider callback arrives as a browser navigation, so a JSON body leaves the user looking at raw error text in the address bar. When the OIDC request context survived the failure we send them back to the login page they started from, carrying error and error_description — the same way /oidc/authorize hands its errors to a login screen. Callers that POST here are APIs, not browsers, and keep getting the JSON body.
